title: LIBRARY GRANTS
full_story:
Illinois Secretary of State and State Librarian Alexi Giannoulias awarded more than $27 million in grants to libraries across Illinois, investing in books, technology, literacy programs, infrastructure improvements and security upgrades.

Among the recipients locally are the Flora Public Library which will get $8,165.10.  The Fairfield Public Library will get $8,301.10, Olney Public Library gets $14,791.70, the Bryan Bennett Library in Salem was awarded $12,379.40, and the Wayne City Public Library gets $1,689.80.

The funding will support public and school libraries serving millions of Illinois residents and students while ensuring communities across the state have access to the resources they need to learn, grow and thrive.  Since taking office in 2023, Giannoulias has directed more than $183 million in grant funding to support public libraries, school libraries and adult literacy programs throughout Illinois.

The Secretary of State’s office also recently awarded more than $1.3 million to 2,524 public school libraries across 660 Illinois school districts.

The Flora Unit School District will receive $1,046.96, The Clay City and the South Central School District will both get $850.

The grants will help schools purchase books, e-books, audiobooks, multilingual materials, technology and other educational resources that support student learning and literacy from kindergarten through 12th grade.

title: FLORA 4th OF JULY
full_story:
Flora has a full day of events scheduled for the 4th of July with all of the events happening at Charley Brown Park.

At 10 am the All American Boy and All American Girl Contest will be on the Kiwanis stage.  The contest is for 3- to 7-year-old boys and girls and the deadline to enter is Wednesday.  Signups are available at the office of Lisa Erbacher Country Financial at 847 East North Avenue across from Rotary Park.

Kenzie’s Sweet Shop will also be on site at 10 am.  From 11 am to 6 pm free inflatables will be open for families, Flora Tourism will also be selling hot dogs and chips.  At 4 pm the food trucks will open, Poe’d Smoked BBQ, The Fair Lady, Colonel Pop, and Krazy Sweet Treats.  From 6 pm to dusk there will be live music by the Rewinds.

Everyone is welcome to bring a lawn chair and enjoy all of the activities.  There will be a shuttle service available to move people from the parking area to the attractions.

Fireworks will be at dusk featuring a 900 shot finale.  Please follow ESDA parking instructions, there will be a shuttle service available to get people from parking to the event.  Flora Tourism could still use a few volunteers.  To volunteer call Arriel Dulaney at the Chamber office at 618-662-5646.

title: SUNDAYS SEVERE WEATHER
full_story:
Severe weather proved to be very active and destructive on Sunday.

According to the National Weather Service in Lincoln and Paducah, as of Wednesday, there were at least 6 tornadoes in our area.

The most severe tornado was the EF 3 near Dix which traveled 15.3 miles.  There were 2 EF 2 tornados reported near Newton.  The Newton south tornado travelled 3.7 miles and the east tornado traveled 2.7 miles.  The other 3 tornadoes in our area have been rated EF 1’s, this includes the Louisville tornado which traveled 4.6 miles.  The other 2 were near Sims and Geff in Wayne County.  The tornado near Geff traveled 3.8 miles and near Sims traveled 1.5 miles.

According to the National Weather Service-Paducah, as of Wednesday, there were at least 15 tornadoes in its 58-county coverage area to our south.  The region’s previous record was set in June 2019 with 13 tornadoes and Jefferson County’s EF3 tornado was the strongest June tornado in the region since June 2, 1990.

title: GAS UTILITY CONSTRUCTION BOOTCAMP
full_story:
Wabash Valley College will host a new Gas Utility Construction Bootcamp, a hands-on training program designed to prepare students for entry-level careers in the natural gas utility and pipeline construction industry.  The bootcamp runs Monday, August 3rd through 14th.

The intensive 2-week course will be held from 8 am to 6 pm at the WVC campus in Mt. Carmel, offering 90 hours of expert training in gas main and service installation, safety protocols, and readiness for Department of Transportation Operator Qualifications (OQ).

Class size is limited to 10 students.  The full bootcamp investment is $1,200, which includes industry-recognized certifications and job placement support.

Applicants must attend all sessions, pass a background check and drug screening, maintain a clean driving record, and be willing to travel or relocate for job opportunities.

People who want to apply for the program can visit https://iecc.edu/gas-utility.

title: GRAZING CONFERENCE
full_story:
The 2026 Heart of America Grazing Conference will be held in Effingham on July 15th and 16th.

It will be the first time in several years Illinois has hosted the five-state rotating conference, according to the Illinois Grazing Lands Coalition.  A few highlights include the following; Farm tour at the operation of Curt Rincker, a Master Grazier Award recipient and past president of the Illinois Beef Association.  Keynote speaker Steve Campbell, known as the “cattle coach,” will discuss cattle genetics and grazing-based production.  Sessions will cover virtual fencing, cropland grazing, bale grazing and multi-species grazing, topics with growing interest among Illinois livestock producers.  And, the “Build a Regenerative Grazing System” competition for ages 14 through 22.

Registration is open at ilgrazinglands.org/events/heart-of-america-grazing-conference.

title: OCC MASSAGE THERAPY SIGN UP
full_story:
Olney Central College’s Massage Therapy Program is accepting new students for Fall 2026.

Designed with busy adults in mind, the program offers convenient evening classes that allow students to pursue a rewarding new career without putting life on hold.  Best of all, the certificate can be completed in just one year.

While enrolled, students gain the skills needed to work in the wellness field of massage therapy, mastering professional massage techniques through hands-on classroom instruction and clinical experience. The program’s clinical opportunities, which are open to the public, provide students with valuable practice working with a variety of clients in a real-world setting.

Olney Central College is recognized as a National Certification Board for Therapeutic Massage & Bodywork (NCBTMB) Assigned School.  This designation confirms that OCC’s Massage Therapy Program meets the high standards of excellence established by the NCBTMB.  It also ensures that after successfully completing state licensure requirements, graduates are eligible to pursue NCBTMB board certification; the highest credential available in the massage therapy profession.

Enrollment is limited.  To reserve a spot, apply by July 15th at www.iecc.edu/apply.

title: COUNTY ACTIVITIES OF EXCELLENCE
full_story:
The American Farm Bureau Federation 2026 County Activities of Excellence (CAE) program is now open for entries to spotlight programs and projects conducted by county Farm Bureaus.

Selected county Farm Bureaus will have the opportunity to showcase their activity at the AFBF Annual Convention, January 8th through 13th in Charlotte, North Carolina.

All applications must be submitted online. Paper or PDF submissions will not be accepted.  Visit the website fb.org/cae and click “APPLY NOW” to access the application portal.  Create a unique user account.  For multi-county submissions, select one county to manage the application.

AFBF will recognize up to 24 individual county activities, including up to four multi-county collaborations.  Winners will receive 4 complimentary registrations to the 2027 AFBF Annual Convention, a booth space at the trade show, and a $4,500 cash stipend to help with travel and exhibit expenses.

title: LEGISLATION FINALLY PASSED
full_story:
Illinois lawmakers finally passed legislation to become the last state in the country to comply with a three-year-old US Supreme Court ruling.

State law allows the government to take an entire property for unpaid property taxes, even when they’re much less than the value of the property.

House Bill 4537 brings the state into compliance with the 2023 high court decision in Tyler v. Hennepin County, which ruled that in taking property, state governments must give owners the value that exceeds the amount owed in taxes.

Since the ruling, local governments in Illinois have been vulnerable to litigation without a clear constitutional process for collecting delinquent property taxes.  Just last month a federal district court ruled that Cook County was in violation of the constitution and potentially on the hook for millions of dollars owed to owners who lost their properties.

If Governor JB Pritzker signs HB 4537, a new public auction would sell property deeds themselves instead of a tax lien that gives the buyer ownership over the property if homeowners fail to pay off the taxes by the redemption deadline.  Counties other than Cook would be allowed to acquire delinquent properties and sell them directly at auction.

The measure also would give the original property owner the right to any sale proceeds over the amount owed in property taxes and also gives an owner three years, up from 2.5, to prevent the sale by paying the unpaid taxes.

HB 4537 also creates a temporary fund to compensate owners who lost their surplus equity.  The fund would pay claims, with the money coming from fees charged to tax buyers.  Counties would remain on the hook for remaining claims if the fund runs out of money.

The bill also establishes a pilot program authorizing Cook County to acquire and directly auction off properties from the first six tax sales rather than first selling the tax liens to private buyers before the redemption period has passed.  The fate of Cook County’s system depends on the success of the pilot program.

title: FAIRGROUNDS TO HOST FREE FISHING DAY
full_story:
Children and teens in Southern Illinois will get a chance to fish for free at an event at the Du Quoin State Fairgrounds in July.

“Fishing is a great sport that exposes kids to nature while teaching them the importance of patience and persistence,” said Jerry Costello II, Director of the Illinois Department of Agriculture.

The Illinois Department of Natural Resources(IDNR) will host the event on Tuesday, July 7, from 9:00 am until 11:30 am.  Participants will meet in front of the Expo Center at 9:00 am.

IDNR officials will provide fishing poles, bait, and basic instructions.  No fishing license is required for participants aged 15 and under.  Registration is required and limited to the first 25 kids who sign up.  Participants are encouraged to bring their own sunscreen, bug spray, water, and a chair.

For more information or to register, call 618-542-1511.  Office hours are Monday through Friday, 8 am to 4 pm, closed on holidays.
